title: One Miss Too Many: Alphabet's Stumble Cools a Hot Tech Rally
body:
Wall Street has long been used to Big Tech beating forecasts, which is exactly why Thursday's **earnings miss** at Alphabet hurt so much. The company, which reported earnings of $2.12 per share against expectations of about $3.01, saw its stock plunge nearly 12%. Microsoft, by contrast, beat estimates and edged higher, suggesting that investors were punishing disappointment rather than dumping tech across the board. Even so, the Nasdaq fell 1.4% to 26,184.72, while the broader S&P 500 slipped only 0.3%, partly because small-cap stocks rallied. Amazon and Intel, both of which reported after the close, also **came under pressure** in late trading.

In Seoul, which had closed hours earlier, the mood had already cooled. After soaring 6.6% on Wednesday, the KOSPI lost 1.2% to 5,937.66 as **profit-taking** set in, and Samsung Electronics dropped 4.1% following its results. The KOSDAQ, whose smaller stocks are more **vulnerable** to sudden swings, fell 2.3%. Although a one-day pullback (되돌림) hardly **wipes out** a 6.6% gain, it shows how quickly optimism can **diminish** once traders lock in (확정하다) profits. Investors who used to treat every dip as a buying chance may now wait for clearer signals. If Apple, which reports next week, also disappoints, a **knee-jerk** sell-off could spread; if it delivers, Thursday may look like nothing more than a brief pause.
ko:
월가는 오랫동안 빅테크가 예상치를 넘는 데 익숙해 있었고, 바로 그래서 목요일 알파벳의 실적 미스가 그렇게 아팠다. 시장 예상 약 3.01달러에 못 미치는 주당순이익 2.12달러를 발표한 이 회사의 주가는 12% 가까이 폭락했다. 반면 마이크로소프트는 예상치를 웃돌며 소폭 올랐는데, 이는 투자자들이 기술주를 통째로 내다 판 것이 아니라 실망에 벌을 준 것임을 시사한다. 그래도 나스닥은 1.4% 내린 26,184.72에 마감했고, 더 넓은 S&P 500은 소형주가 오른 덕분에 0.3% 하락에 그쳤다. 장 마감 후 실적을 낸 아마존과 인텔도 시간외 거래에서 압박을 받았다.

몇 시간 앞서 장을 마친 서울에서는 분위기가 이미 식어 있었다. 수요일 6.6% 급등한 코스피는 차익 실현이 나오며 1.2% 내린 5,937.66에 마감했고, 삼성전자는 실적 발표 후 4.1% 떨어졌다. 작은 종목이 많아 급등락에 더 취약한 코스닥은 2.3% 하락했다. 하루짜리 되돌림이 6.6% 상승을 지워 버리는 것은 아니지만, 트레이더들이 이익을 확정하기 시작하면 낙관이 얼마나 빨리 줄어드는지를 보여 준다. 예전엔 하락할 때마다 매수 기회로 여기던 투자자들도 이제는 더 분명한 신호를 기다릴지 모른다. 다음 주 실적을 내는 애플마저 실망을 준다면 반사적인 매도가 번질 수 있고, 기대에 부응한다면 목요일은 잠깐의 숨 고르기로 보일 것이다.

vocab.en_easy: When a company's profit comes in lower than what analysts expected.
vocab.ex: One earnings miss was enough to knock the stock down 12% in a single day.

vocab.en_easy: Selling a stock after it has gone up, to lock in the gain.
vocab.ex: After a 6.6% jump, a little profit-taking the next day is pretty normal.

vocab.en_easy: Done quickly and automatically, without thinking carefully.
vocab.ex: My knee-jerk reaction was to sell everything, but I waited a day and calmed down.

vocab.en_easy: Easily hurt or affected by something bad.
vocab.ex: My knees are vulnerable to injury, so I always warm up before I run.

vocab.en_easy: To become smaller or less strong.
vocab.ex: My motivation tends to diminish in winter, so I sign up for a race to keep going.

vocab.en_easy: To be pushed down or be forced to deal with difficulty.
vocab.ex: Chip stocks came under pressure after the weak forecast.

vocab.en_easy: To remove or destroy something completely.
vocab.ex: One bad week wiped out all the gains I'd made since summer.

grammar.point: used to + 동사원형 vs be used to + -ing(명사)
grammar.quote: Wall Street has long been used to Big Tech beating forecasts … / Investors who used to treat every dip as a buying chance …
grammar.explain_ko: used to + 동사원형 = '(예전엔) ~하곤 했다(지금은 아님)'. be(get/grow) used to + 명사·동명사 = '~에 익숙하다'. 뒤의 to가 전치사라서 동명사(-ing)가 온다. 본문 첫 문장 Big Tech beating은 동명사 beating의 의미상 주어가 Big Tech. 수능 어법 단골: be used to see ✗ → be used to seeing ✓ / (참고) be used to + 동사원형 = '~하는 데 사용되다'(수동태).
examples: I'm used to checking the market before breakfast, but I used to sleep in until noon in college.
(OPIc) I used to hate running, but now I'm so used to it that I actually feel weird if I skip a day.

grammar.point: 관계대명사 계속적 용법 (, which / , who / , whose / both of which)
grammar.quote: The company, which reported earnings of $2.12 per share … / Amazon and Intel, both of which reported after the close, … / The KOSDAQ, whose smaller stocks are more vulnerable …
grammar.explain_ko: 콤마 뒤 관계사절은 앞 명사를 '골라내는' 게 아니라 '덧붙여 설명'한다(= and it / and they). that은 계속적 용법에 못 쓴다(, that ✗). 부분표현은 both/some/all of which(whom)처럼 전치사 of 뒤 목적격. 소유는 whose + 명사.
examples: Samsung, which reported its results on Thursday, fell 4.1%.
(OPIc) I usually go to Bukhansan, which is about thirty minutes from my place, with my college friends, most of whom are into hiking now.

tense.sentence: Wall Street has long been used to Big Tech beating forecasts.
tense.why_ko: 과거부터 지금까지 '쭉 익숙해 있던' 상태 — long과 함께 계속 용법. 특정 과거 시점이 없어서 과거형이 아니다.

tense.sentence: In Seoul, which had closed hours earlier, the mood had already cooled.
tense.why_ko: 미국 장(과거 기준 시점)보다 서울 장 마감·분위기 냉각이 '더 먼저' 일어났으므로 had p.p.

review.q: Alphabet's profit ______ what analysts had expected, so the stock dropped almost 12%.
choices: made up for
fell short of
shook off
hinged on
review.exp_ko: fall short of = ~에 못 미치다. 주가가 떨어진 이유이니 '예상에 못 미쳤다'. made up for(만회했다)·shook off(털어냈다)는 하락과 반대 논리, hinged on(~에 달려 있었다)은 '이익이 예상에 달려 있다'로 말이 안 됨.

review.q: 다음 문장과 뜻이 가장 가까운 것은? "Whether the rebound continues hinges on Apple's results next week."
choices: Apple's results next week will be delayed by the rebound.
The rebound has already been confirmed by Apple's results.
Whether the rebound continues depends on Apple's results next week.
Apple's results next week matter little to the rebound.
review.exp_ko: hinge on = depend on(~에 달려 있다). ①은 인과 방향이 반대, ②는 이미 확정(시제 오류), ④는 '별 상관없다'로 정반대.

review.w: take ~ with a grain of salt
review.q: The rumor about a surprise rate cut spread fast online, but I ______ because it had no official source.
choices: took it with a grain of salt
took it to heart
took it for granted
took it in stride
review.exp_ko: take ~ with a grain of salt = 반쯤 걸러 듣다. '공식 출처가 없어서'와 맞는 건 의심하며 듣기. to heart(진지하게 받아들이다)·for granted(당연시하다)는 because 이유와 반대, in stride(침착하게 넘기다)는 나쁜 일을 담담히 견딘다는 뜻이라 소문 '신뢰도'와 무관.

quiz.q:
[어휘] 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 문맥상 가장 적절한 것은?
"Although a one-day pullback hardly ______ a 6.6% gain, it shows how quickly optimism can diminish once traders lock in profits."
choices: phases out
sorts out
rules out
wipes out
quiz.exp_ko: '하루 되돌림이 6.6% 상승을 ___하진 못하지만'이므로 '싹 지워 버리다' = wipes out. phase out(단계적으로 없애다)은 정책·제품에, sort out(해결·정리하다)은 문제에, rule out(배제하다)은 가능성에 쓰는 동사라 '상승분'과 짝이 안 맞는다.

quiz.q:
[어법] 다음 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?
"Alphabet, ①which had beaten forecasts for years, shocked investors ②who are used to see Big Tech deliver good news. ③Shaken by the miss, traders sold the stock, ④whereas Microsoft's shares edged higher."
choices: ① which
② who are used to see
③ Shaken
④ whereas
quiz.exp_ko: be used to의 to는 전치사 → 동명사 seeing이어야 한다(be used to see ✗). ① 콤마 뒤 계속적 용법 which ✓(that 불가 자리), ③ 트레이더가 '충격을 받은' 수동 관계라 과거분사 Shaken ✓, ④ 두 절 대조 접속사 whereas ✓.

quiz.q: [요지] 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? (본문 전체)
choices: A single disappointing report can quickly cool investor optimism, though one day's drop does not erase a strong rally.
Big Tech stocks have become too vulnerable to recommend, so investors should sell all tech shares now.
Korean stocks fell because of Alphabet's results, which were released before the Seoul market opened.
Small-cap stocks are now safer than large tech stocks because they rallied while the Nasdaq fell.
quiz.exp_ko: 글은 '실망 하나 → 낙관이 빨리 식는다, 하지만 하루 하락이 6.6% 랠리를 지우진 않는다'가 축. ②는 '전부 팔라'는 과장(본문은 기술주 전반 매도가 아니라고 함), ③은 서울이 몇 시간 '먼저' 마감했다는 본문과 시간 순서가 반대, ④는 소형주 반등 한 줄을 일반화한 것.

quiz.q: [내용 일치·추론] 본문의 숫자로 판단할 때 옳은 것은?
choices: The S&P 500 fell more in percentage terms than the KOSPI did.
Alphabet's shares fell by less than four times the Nasdaq's decline.
The KOSDAQ's percentage drop was almost twice that of the KOSPI.
Alphabet's actual earnings per share were about 30 cents below expectations.
quiz.exp_ko: 코스닥 −2.3% vs 코스피 −1.2% → 2.3÷1.2 ≈ 1.9배 = 거의 2배 ✓. ① S&P −0.3%는 코스피 −1.2%보다 작다 ✗ ② 알파벳 약 −12%는 나스닥 −1.4%의 8배 넘음 ✗ ④ 3.01 − 2.12 = 0.89달러 = 약 89센트 ✗(30센트로 착각하면 함정).

talk.topic: One bad report — 알파벳 12% 급락, 기술주 전체를 팔아야 하나
talk.setting_ko: 금요일 아침 출근길, 투자하는 회사 동료와 지하철에서 밤사이 미국장 얘기를 나눈다.

dialogue.en: Did you see Alphabet last night? It took a real beating — down almost 12%.
dialogue.ko: 어젯밤 알파벳 봤어? 제대로 두들겨 맞았더라 — 거의 12% 빠졌어.

dialogue.en: Yeah, I woke up to it. Their profit missed by a mile. Kind of a reality check for the whole AI story.
dialogue.ko: 응, 일어나자마자 봤어. 이익이 한참 못 미쳤대. AI 이야기 전체에 현실을 일깨우는 일이랄까.

dialogue.en: So should I dump my tech stocks? My gut says sell.
dialogue.ko: 그럼 기술주 다 팔아야 하나? 직감은 팔라는데.

dialogue.en: I'd hold on. Microsoft actually went up, so it's not like the market is brushing off all of Big Tech.
dialogue.ko: 난 버티겠어. 마이크로소프트는 오히려 올랐잖아, 시장이 빅테크를 통째로 외면하는 건 아니야.

dialogue.en: True. But buying Alphabet now feels like trying to catch a falling knife.
dialogue.ko: 맞아. 근데 지금 알파벳을 사는 건 떨어지는 칼날 잡는 느낌이야.

dialogue.en: Exactly. It's too early to call. Let's see what Apple says next week.
dialogue.ko: 그러니까. 판단하기엔 아직 일러. 다음 주 애플이 뭐라는지 보자.

dialogue.en: Fair enough. No knee-jerk moves for me, then.
dialogue.ko: 그래. 그럼 나도 즉흥적으로 움직이진 않을게.

expressions.ex: My portfolio took a real beating in October.

expressions.ko: 현실을 일깨우는 일, 정신 차리게 하는 계기
expressions.when_ko: 기대가 너무 컸다는 걸 깨닫게 되는 일
expressions.ex: Failing my first mock test was a reality check.

expressions.when_ko: 나쁜 소식·조언을 신경 안 쓸 때
expressions.ex: The market brushed off the bad news and kept going up.

expressions.ko: 떨어지는 칼날을 잡다(급락 중에 성급히 매수)
expressions.when_ko: 폭락하는 종목을 바로 사려 할 때 경고
expressions.ex: Buying right after a 12% drop is like trying to catch a falling knife.
Who's going to win the game? It's too early to call.

your_turn.q_en: If a stock you own suddenly dropped 12% in one day, what would you do and why?
your_turn.hint_ko: If ~ dropped, I would ~ (가정법 과거) → 이유 2개(실적 확인·분할 매수 등) → 'It's too early to call' 활용
your_turn.sample_answer: Honestly, my knee-jerk reaction would be to sell, but I'd try not to. First, I'd check why it fell — was it a one-time miss or a real change in the business? If it was just one bad quarter, I'd hold on, because selling in a panic usually means selling at the bottom. I wouldn't buy more right away either, since that feels like catching a falling knife. It's too early to call after one day, so I'd wait a week and then decide.

talk.topic: 카페에서 음료가 잘못 나왔을 때 — 정중하게 바꿔 달라기 (Background Survey #12 카페/커피전문점)
talk.setting_ko: 단골 카페에서 아이스 오트라테를 시켰는데 뜨거운 우유 라테가 나왔다. 바리스타에게 말한다.

dialogue.en: Excuse me, sorry to bother you. I think there's been a mix-up with my order.
dialogue.ko: 저기요, 번거롭게 해서 죄송한데요. 제 주문이 좀 바뀐 것 같아요.

dialogue.en: Oh, really? Let me take a look. What did you order?
dialogue.ko: 아, 그래요? 한번 볼게요. 뭐 시키셨어요?

dialogue.en: I ordered an iced oat latte, but this one's hot and made with regular milk.
dialogue.ko: 아이스 오트라테 시켰는데, 이건 따뜻하고 일반 우유로 만든 거네요.

dialogue.en: You're right, my bad. Would you mind waiting a couple of minutes while I remake it?
dialogue.ko: 맞네요, 제 실수예요. 다시 만드는 동안 2분 정도 기다려 주시겠어요?

dialogue.en: No worries, take your time. It's pretty busy in here this morning.
dialogue.ko: 괜찮아요, 천천히 하세요. 오늘 아침 엄청 바쁘네요.

dialogue.en: Thanks for being so understanding. Here's a cookie on the house for the trouble.
dialogue.ko: 이해해 주셔서 감사해요. 번거롭게 해 드려서 쿠키는 서비스로 드릴게요.

dialogue.en: Oh, that's so nice of you. Thanks a lot!

expressions.en: I think there's been a mix-up.
expressions.when_ko: 주문·예약·자리가 잘못됐을 때 부드럽게 말 꺼내기
expressions.ex: I think there's been a mix-up with our reservation.

expressions.when_ko: 직원·낯선 사람에게 말 걸 때 쿠션어
expressions.ex: Sorry to bother you, but is there a restroom here?
Would you mind turning the music down a little?
The owner gave us dessert on the house.
Thanks for being so understanding about the delay.

your_turn.q_en: Tell me about a time when something went wrong at a café or restaurant. What happened, and how did you deal with it?
your_turn.hint_ko: 배경(언제·어디) → 문제(I think there's been a mix-up) → 해결(Would you mind ~?) → 결과·느낌. 과거 시제 유지
your_turn.sample_answer: A few months ago, I went to a café near my office and ordered an iced americano. But when I took a sip, it was super sweet — they'd given me someone else's vanilla latte. So I went back to the counter and said, 'Sorry to bother you, but I think there's been a mix-up.' The barista apologized right away and made me a new one. She even gave me a cookie on the house. Honestly, I wasn't upset at all. Mistakes happen, and the way she handled it actually made me like that place even more.

opic.survey_topic: 금요일 — 셀프 소개 + 주간 복습 콤보 (헬스 #51 · 국내 여행 #56)

combo.q_en: Let's start the interview now. Tell me a little bit about yourself.
combo.q_ko: 이제 인터뷰를 시작하죠. 자기소개를 해 주세요.
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(이름 대신 한 줄 정체성: I'd say I'm someone who ~) → 본문 2~3포인트: ①하는 일·사는 곳 ②취미(서베이 주제와 연결 — 헬스·여행으로 다음 문항 깔아 두기) ③요즘 관심사(주식·영어 공부) → 마무리 한 줄. 60~90초. 채점 포인트: 문단 길이로 이어 말하기, 현재·현재완료 섞기(I've been ~ing). ※ 답변의 직업·사는 곳은 자기 실제 정보로 바꿔 외운다.
combo.model_answer: Okay, so, let me start with the basics. I live in Seoul, and I work at a company there — it's a pretty typical office job, you know, lots of meetings and emails. But outside of work, I'd say I'm someone who really likes to stay active. I go to the gym four or five times a week, and lately I've been getting into running, too. Believe it or not, I used to be a total couch potato back in college, so that's a big change for me. Another thing I'm into these days is investing. I started following the stock market about a year ago, and now I'm used to checking the news every morning before work. It's kind of become a habit. Oh, and I also love short trips around Korea — whenever I get a long weekend, I try to get out of the city. Um, what else... I guess I'm also working on my English, which is why I'm here today! So yeah, all in all, I'm a pretty busy but happy person.

key_phrases.en: Let me start with the basics.
I used to be a total couch potato.
key_phrases.ko: 예전엔 완전 집돌이(소파에만 붙어 있는 사람)였어요.

combo.level_up_ko: IM은 '이름·나이·직업' 나열, IH는 취미를 이유와 함께 문단으로, AL은 used to(과거) → now(현재) → 계획(미래)까지 시제를 오가며 '변화'로 엮는다.

combo.q_en: In your background survey, you indicated that you go to the gym. Tell me about your typical workout routine. What do you do first, and what do you do after that? Please tell me in as much detail as possible.
combo.q_ko: 서베이에서 헬스장에 간다고 하셨는데요. 평소 운동 루틴을 말해 주세요. 처음에 뭘 하고 그다음엔 뭘 하나요? 최대한 자세히요.
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(얼마나 자주·언제) → 순서 3단계: 워밍업 → 메인(분할: 하체 날 — quads·hamstrings·glutes / 등 날 — lats, deadlift) → 마무리(스트레칭·기록) → 마무리 한 줄(왜 이 루틴을 지키는지). First / After that / Once I'm done / Finally 같은 순서 연결어로 문단을 만든다. 근육 이름이 '구체적 묘사' 점수.
combo.model_answer: Well, I usually work out right after work, around seven, about four or five days a week. I follow a split routine, so what I do depends on the day. First, no matter what, I warm up on the treadmill for about ten minutes, just a light jog to get my heart rate up. After that, I move on to the main lifts. On leg day, for example, I start with squats, which really hit my quads and glutes, and then I do Romanian deadlifts for my hamstrings. On back day, it's mostly deadlifts, pull-ups, and rows for my lats. I try to follow progressive overload, so every week I add a little weight or do one or two more reps. Actually, wait — I should mention I always log every set in an app, because otherwise I forget what I did last time. Once I'm done lifting, I stretch for five or ten minutes, especially my hips. Finally, I grab a protein shake on the way home. It sounds kind of repetitive, I know, but having a set routine keeps me from skipping workouts.

key_phrases.en: I follow a split routine, so what I do depends on the day.
key_phrases.ko: 분할 루틴이라 그날그날 하는 게 달라요.

key_phrases.en: ~ really hits my quads and glutes
I try to follow progressive overload.

combo.level_up_ko: IM은 '스쿼트 해요, 벤치 해요' 나열, IH는 First/After that 순서와 근육 이름, AL은 'Actually, wait —' 자기수정과 '왜 그 순서인지(이유)'까지 넣는다.

combo.q_en: I'd like to know about a memorable trip you took somewhere in your country. Where did you go and who did you go with? What happened during the trip that made it so special? Tell me everything from beginning to end.
combo.q_ko: 국내에서 기억에 남는 여행 이야기를 듣고 싶어요. 어디에 누구와 갔나요? 무슨 일이 있어서 특별했나요? 처음부터 끝까지 말해 주세요.
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(언제·어디·누구 한 문장) → 본문: 기대했던 계획 → 예상 밖 사건(과거완료 had p.p.로 '이미 ~했었는데') → 대처·반전 → 마무리(그 여행이 남긴 것, 지금의 습관과 연결). 과거 시제를 끝까지 유지하는 게 IH 핵심, 감정 단어(I was so frustrated / relieved) 2개 이상.
combo.model_answer: Let me think... Oh, I know. Last spring, I went to Yeosu with two of my college friends. We'd been talking about that trip for months, so we were super excited. The plan was simple: eat a ton of seafood, ride the cable car, and see the night view by the sea. But on the first day, it poured all afternoon, and the cable car was shut down because of the wind. We were so frustrated, you know, because that was the main reason we went. So instead, we just found a tiny local restaurant and ordered way too much food — grilled fish, crab marinated in soy sauce, all of it. The owner, who was super friendly, told us about a quiet beach nearby that tourists don't usually know about. The next morning, the sky was totally clear, so we went there and it was, like, empty and beautiful. Honestly, it's hard to put into words how relaxing it felt. Looking back, the rain kind of turned out to be a good thing. Now whenever plans fall apart on a trip, I just tell myself, 'Something better might come up.'

key_phrases.en: We'd been talking about ~ for months.
It's hard to put into words how ~
~ turned out to be a good thing

combo.level_up_ko: IM은 '갔다·먹었다·좋았다', IH는 문제-대처-결과 이야기 구조, AL은 과거완료(We'd been ~)와 계속적 관계사(, who was ~)로 문장을 길게 잇고 마지막에 교훈을 현재형으로 던진다.

opic.practice_ko: 오늘은 금요일 복습: ① 자기소개 60초를 녹음 → 끝에 헬스·여행을 한 줄씩 깔았는지 확인 ② 운동 루틴 답변을 대본 없이 다시 녹음하고 First/After that/Once I'm done/Finally 4개를 다 썼는지 체크.
